description: Dogs descend from wolves and were domesticated by hunter-gatherers long before farming. Genetic estimates of when the lineages separated range from about 15,000 to over 30,000 years ago, and single versus multiple origins are debated. A puppy buried with two people at Bonn-Oberkassel, Germany, about 14,200 years ago had survived repeated distemper, apparently through human care.

claims: Divergence estimates vary widely; single or multiple origins debated
Bonn-Oberkassel dated about 14,200 years ago; burial with two people
Distemper episodes; survival argued to imply human care

uncertainty: Date and place(s) of domestication are unresolved; genetic divergence dates are upper bounds, not domestication dates, and wolf-dog interbreeding complicates them. Older candidate dogs (Goyet, Razboinichya) are disputed.
